Mission ISRO.name: Mission ISRO with Harsha Bhogle
Mission ISRO.description: Born into violence, poverty and the desolation of colonial exploitation, newly independent India was a nation working hard to find its footing. The story of India’s space programme is an unlikely one, filled with impossible odds, extraordinary visionaries like Vikram Sarabhai, Homi Bhabha, Satish Dhawan, and A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. Narrated with gripping passion by Harsha Bhogle, with original score by Raghu Dixit.

episodes.title: Episode 1: Saare Jahan Se Achcha
episodes.description: Opens with the historic 1984 exchange between Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and Rakesh Sharma. Harsha Bhogle takes listeners back to newly independent India, introducing Dr. Vikram Sarabhai and Dr. Homi J. Bhabha.

episodes.title: Episode 2: A Church in Thumba
episodes.description: Establishing the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) in a Kerala fishing village and operating out of St. Mary Magdalene Church.

episodes.title: Episode 3: Bicycles and Bullock Carts
episodes.description: The iconic story of transporting rocket components, nose-cones, and payloads on bicycles and bullock carts across sandy shores.

episodes.title: Episode 4: The First Launch - Nike Apache
episodes.description: November 21, 1963: The first sodium vapor sounding rocket ascends into the twilight sky over the Arabian Sea, marking India's entry into the space age.

episodes.title: Episode 5: SITE - Television to the Villages
episodes.description: The groundbreaking Satellite Instructional Television Experiment (SITE), delivering direct satellite broadcast education to over 2,400 rural Indian villages.

episodes.title: Episode 6: Aryabhata Ascending
episodes.description: April 19, 1975: India's first satellite Aryabhata launches from Kapustin Yar aboard a Soviet Kosmos-3M launch vehicle.

episodes.title: Episode 7: The Birth of SLV-3 & Kalam
episodes.description: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam is appointed project director of India's first satellite launch vehicle, rallying a young team against immense technological hurdles.

episodes.title: Episode 8: Computer, put a hold! Don't launch it.
episodes.description: August 10, 1979: The nerve-wracking countdown of SLV-3's maiden experimental flight, a critical computer warning, and the lessons of failure.

episodes.title: Episode 9: Rohini Reaches Orbit
episodes.description: July 18, 1980: Jubilation as SLV-3 E2 successfully places the Rohini RS-1 satellite into orbit, establishing India as the world's 6th spacefaring nation.

episodes.title: Episode 10: APPLE of Our Eyes
episodes.description: The Ariane Passenger Payload Experiment (APPLE) communications satellite, tested for antenna interference in the bed of an unmotorized wooden bullock cart.

episodes.title: Episode 11: Sar Pe Laal Topi Russi
episodes.description: Navigating Cold War geopolitics, technical cooperation with Moscow, and the dramatic quest to acquire cryogenic rocket propulsion technology.

episodes.title: Episode 12: The Workhorse - PSLV
episodes.description: The design and flight test of the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, developing what would become one of the most reliable rockets in space exploration history.

episodes.title: Episode 13: Sanctions & The Espionage Case
episodes.description: US sanctions on cryogenic technology transfers, and the dark turbulence of the false 1994 ISRO espionage case.

episodes.title: Episode 14: Eyes in the Skies
episodes.description: How India built one of the largest constellations of remote sensing and earth observation satellites, monitoring crops, borders, and ocean cyclones.

episodes.title: Episode 15: The Naughty Boy Rocket
episodes.description: The formidable challenge of mastering cryogenic propulsion, the temperamental early GSLV flights, and the persistence that tamed the rocket.

episodes.title: Episode 16: Beyond Earth - To The Moon & Mars
episodes.description: From finding water molecules on the Moon with Chandrayaan-1 to the historic Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) and the dawn of Gaganyaan.
